body.statement: Shu--Wang--Li, Theorem 2, gives for their scalar \(\operatorname{PNS}(k)\) the lower pieces \(0\), \(\sum_ja_j-k+1\), and \(b_i+\sum_{j\ne i}(a_j+p_j-b_j)-k+1\), and the upper pieces \(\sum_{j\leq k}b_j+\sum_{j>k}p_j\), the margins \(a_j\), and \(\sum_{j\in S}(a_j-b_j)/(|S|-1)\) for \(|S|\geq2\).  Their Theorems 6 and 7 respectively give zero-probability padding for unequal finite alphabets and replacement of queried outcome labels.

source.verbatim_statement: Theorem 2 (Probability of necessity and sufficiency(k) (PNS(k))). Suppose variable X has n values x_{1},...,x_{n} and Y has n values y_{1},...,y_{n}, k\leq n, then P({y_{1}}_{x_{1}},...,{y_{k}}_{x_{k}}) is bounded below by \max\{0, \sum_{j=1}^{k}P({y_j}_{x_j})-k+1, \sum_{1\leq j\leq k,j\neq i}[P({y_j}_{x_j})+P(x_j)-P(x_j,y_j)]+P(x_i,y_i)-k+1, i\in\{1,...,k\}\} and bounded above by \min\{\sum_{j=1}^{k}P(x_j,y_j)+\sum_{j=k+1}^{n}P(x_j), P({y_j}_{x_j}) for j\in\{1,...,k\}, (1/m)[\sum_{j=0}^{m}P({y_{t_j}}_{x_{t_j}})-P(x_{t_j},y_{t_j})] for m\in\{1,...,k-1\}, t_j\in\{1,...,k\}\}. Theorem 6 (Equivalence classes in probabilities of causation). For k\leq m<n, adjoining outcome values y_l prime with P({y_l prime}_{x_j})=0 and P(y_l prime)=0 for m+1\leq l\leq n preserves the bounds; for k\leq n<m, adjoining treatment values x_l prime with P({y_j}_{x_l prime})=0, P({y_m}_{x_l prime})=1, and P(x_l prime)=0 for n+1\leq l\leq m and 1\leq j\leq m-1 preserves the bounds, while the original cells retain their probabilities. Theorem 7 (Replaceability in probabilities of causation). The bounds with {y_i}_{x_i} replaced by {y_hat_i}_{x_i} can be obtained by making the same replacement in the bounds of P({y_1}_{x_1},...,{y_k}_{x_k}), for any 1\leq i\leq n.
